title: I thought the Pixel 11’s Magic Capture would be perfect for concerts. I was wrong
summary: Magic Capture is great, but only under certain circumstances.
body: I’ve been using the Google Pixel 11 series for well over a month now, but Magic Capture was the one feature that caught my eye before I even held the new phones. Google’s reputation for delivering incredible Pixel camera experiences through software features is proven — Add Me, Auto Best Take , and Camera Coach are recent examples. Many of these camera modes, however, become something you try once or twice and then proceed to forget about . Magic Capture is a Pixel 11 feature that uses Gemini models to analyze roughly 400 video frames and select the best ones to save as photos. As someone who often goes to sporting events and concerts, I thought this feature could’ve been useful enough to keep a Pixel 11 in my pocket year-round. So, I spent weeks testing Magic Capture at the zoo, at a concert, and even at a yo-yo tournament.

title: I’ve been a smart home user for 10 years, and the Apple HomeView looks like a game-changer
summary: From intrusive ads to clunky software, the smart home landscape has a lot of room to improve. The HomeView could help.
body: Smart displays are a category that, to me, have always felt like they’re on the cusp of being the next big thing for the smart home. I was excited when I first got my Nest Hub . The idea that I could control connected devices with a tap, without having to shout commands at a speaker or pull out my phone, was incredibly appealing. Want to turn off the lights? Just tap a button. Simple, practical. Fast forward to today, and it’s hard not to feel like the category has gone nowhere. Google’s Nest Hub displays are getting long in the tooth, while Amazon’s Echo Show lineup has become increasingly difficult to recommend when so much of the screen real estate is effectively used as a digital billboard. For something that’s supposed to make your home more convenient, that’s a pretty disappointing state of affairs.

title: I’ve been using an AI agent for a month, and I’m both impressed and terrified
summary: Instinct AI is extremely good, with some big caveats.
body: We’ve reached a pretty interesting point with AI. For the longest time, I’ve mostly used AI tools to ask questions or to write emails and summarize long PDFs. But AI agents are starting to change that. If you’re unfamiliar with the difference between an AI chatbot and an AI agent, it’s pretty simple. While a chatbot mostly gives you answers or helps you figure out how to do something, an AI agent can actually perform those tasks for you. For example, instead of asking AI to draft an email, you can ask an agent to find the relevant information, write the email, and send it on your behalf.
